scenario_text: Restore a deleted department file from the previous night's successful backup after the file owner confirms the required restore point.
Change the recovery point objective for a critical application from 24 hours to 4 hours without changing backup frequency, storage, or replication design.
Validate that a critical server's scheduled backup completed successfully and that the expected restore point appears in the backup catalog.
Shorten immutable backup retention from 30 days to 3 days so backup storage can be reclaimed more quickly.
Add a supported file server to the existing immutable backup policy using the same retention and copy settings as similar servers.
Stop backing up a low-use production application because no restore requests have been received in the last two years.
A quarterly DR test reveals one documentation error, but all recovery steps succeed after the documented address is corrected.
A replication job falls behind during a network outage but catches up within the approved RPO once connectivity returns.
A business owner requests restoration of data older than the approved retention period and asks the backup team to locate an undocumented copy.
A DR test restores the database successfully, but external authentication fails; the owner asks to record the test as fully successful because the core data was recovered.
Deploy a new Windows server using the agency's approved virtual-machine template, standard network segment, and existing backup policy.
Move a production application from the existing virtualization platform to a new cloud-hosting service that has not been reviewed for identity, logging, backup, or data-location requirements.
During a scheduled maintenance window, move a virtual machine to another host in the same approved cluster so a host can be rebooted for firmware maintenance.
Reconfigure a two-node production cluster to run both nodes in the same physical rack even though the current design separates them to reduce common failure risk.
Restart a non-clustered development server during an approved maintenance window after confirming no active user sessions and documenting the change.
Continue operating a production server after the vendor ends support for its operating system because the application team cannot upgrade for another year.
A production VM shows high CPU during month-end processing. Monitoring confirms the pattern is expected, capacity remains within the approved threshold, and no user impact is reported.
A file server is short on space. The approved storage pool has capacity, but the request asks for an increase much larger than recent growth would justify.
A legacy application cannot tolerate the agency's planned network segmentation, and the owner asks to leave it on a broad shared subnet indefinitely.
A production server needs more CPU, but the cluster is already near its approved capacity threshold and adding resources may affect failover capability.
Verify that a proposed server meets the published CPU, memory, warranty, and support requirements in the solicitation.
Remove the encryption-at-rest requirement from an RFP because several vendors say meeting it will increase cost.
Verify that a vendor's proposed storage platform supports the interface and capacity requirements already published in the solicitation.
Accept a vendor architecture that requires the agency to expose an internal management interface directly to the public internet because the vendor says it simplifies support.
Request clarification from a bidder whose response does not specify whether software updates are included during the support term.
Permit a vendor to begin additional implementation work not included in the executed contract because the work is needed to meet the project schedule.
A vendor response uses different terminology for an encryption feature, and the supporting documentation shows it satisfies the stated requirement.
A vendor support engineer needs temporary remote access during implementation, and the solicitation already requires agency-approved time-limited access with logging.
A vendor proposes storing diagnostic copies of agency data in its support environment for troubleshooting, but the solicitation does not authorize that use.
A vendor can meet the required four-hour support response only if the agency purchases a premium service tier not included in the evaluated price.
Disable a terminated employee's account and remove standard group memberships using the documented offboarding checklist.
Allow a vendor to keep a permanent administrator account on a production server so support staff can connect whenever needed.
Investigate a failed-login alert and close it after confirming the user mistyped a password several times and no other suspicious activity is present.
Turn off centralized logging for a production application because the log volume is increasing storage costs.
Enable the approved screen-lock policy on newly deployed workstations using the existing endpoint-management baseline.
Exclude a critical application server from endpoint protection because the vendor says its software performs better without it.
A user reports repeated MFA prompts after changing phones. The approved support process resets the user's MFA registration after identity verification.
A privileged administrator needs temporary elevated access for a documented maintenance task, and the existing process provides time-limited approval and logging.
A vendor asks to whitelist an entire external IP range because its support staff may connect from multiple offices.
A legacy application supports MFA for administrators but not standard users, and the owner asks to exempt the entire application from MFA policy.
